business_problem: BBVA needed to prove that AI agents could initiate consumer purchases securely within existing payment infrastructure while preserving cardholder consent, issuer oversight, and EU Strong Customer Authentication compliance.
solution_summary: BBVA used Visa Intelligent Commerce in a live agentic commerce test to let an AI agent initiate a purchase on behalf of a cardholder using real card credentials and an active merchant environment. The transaction was processed on existing payment infrastructure rather than a simulated sandbox, with tokenisation protecting credentials as the payment request entered the flow and real-time fraud monitoring checking the transaction before authorisation. To satisfy European Strong Customer Authentication requirements, BBVA added Visa Payment Passkeys so the cardholder could approve the online payment biometrically instead of by password or SMS. The implementation linked AI systems, merchant systems, issuer controls and Visa security protections into a single production-style path, showing that agent-initiated payments can be served securely and compliantly at scale even though the source does not describe storage internals or model architecture.

solution_components.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce
solution_components.role: Enabled the live agentic commerce transaction and connected the AI-initiated purchase to the secure payment infrastructure.

solution_components.name: real-time fraud monitoring
solution_components.role: Checked the transaction in real time to keep the agent-initiated payment secure.

solution_components.name: Visa Payment Passkeys

data_flow: An AI agent initiated a purchase request for a cardholder, the request was routed through Visa Intelligent Commerce using tokenised card credentials and real-time fraud monitoring, and the cardholder then authenticated the payment with Visa Payment Passkeys to satisfy SCA before the transaction was completed with the active merchant and issuer systems.

business_outcome: BBVA completed its first live AI agent-initiated card transaction and showed that agentic payments can run in a real merchant environment using existing infrastructure, cardholder consent controls, and current regulatory protections.
